case-053.notes: BOUNDARY CASE: naive expectation is 'Cascade Supplies' should fuzzy-match 'Cascade Office Supply' and judge-approve; actual normalized similarity (0.703) falls just under FUZZY_MATCH_CUTOFF=0.72, so find_vendor() returns no match at all and it hits UNKNOWN_VENDOR (blocking error) instead of ever reaching judge. See eval_report.md investigation.

case-054.notes: BOUNDARY CASE: unit price moved exactly 10.0% (22.00 -> 24.20); naive golden label assumed a round-number 10% jump would still get a second look, but validate.py's PRICE_DRIFT check is strictly '> 0.10', so exactly 10.0% does not trigger it and the case auto-posts with zero issues. See eval_report.md investigation.

case-055.notes: BOUNDARY CASE: naive golden label assumed confidence must be STRICTLY greater than 0.85 to auto-approve; judge.py's documented threshold is confidence >= 0.85, so this case actually auto-posts. On review this is a golden-label authoring error, not a system bug — see eval_report.md investigation.

case-056.notes: BOUNDARY CASE: invoice number 'INV-0500' coincidentally matches a ledger entry already posted for a DIFFERENT vendor (Acme Corp). Naive golden label assumed any invoice-number collision should be flagged; actual duplicate check is scoped to (vendor_name, invoice_number) pairs, per the DUPLICATE_INVOICE check in validate.py, so a different vendor with the same number does not trigger it and the case auto-posts. This is a real, documented scope limitation (see decision-log.md) rather than a bug — cross-vendor number collisions are common in practice and vendor-scoping is the correct default, but it's worth knowing the check won't catch this class.
